story_title: As the assigned Event Coordinator, I want to request more than one venue for the same event so that a larger event can use several spaces at the same time, such as an auditorium and breakout rooms

acceptance_criteria.text: The Coordinator can submit more than one venue booking request for the same event (and the same session, where applicable), including for the same date and times.
Each venue's availability and conflicts are checked independently; one venue being unavailable does not block a request for another.
Bookings for the same event at different venues do not conflict with each other.
The same venue cannot be requested twice for the same event for overlapping times.
Each booking request is reviewed by Venue Staff separately and has its own status.
All of the event's venue bookings are shown together on the event, each with its venue, times and status.
Given one of the event's venue bookings is rejected, changed, withdrawn or released, when that happens, then the event's other venue bookings are unchanged.
An event with a single venue booking continues to behave as it does today.

open_questions: Written 2026-10-10, before any SPM-81 code. Checked against Week 7 Customer Changes (Change #3), the discussion logs up to 20261006 (#41, #109, #128) and the code on main. Finding: the request rules already checked one venue at a time and exempted the event's own bookings (SPM-42, SPM-44, SPM-93), so nothing stopped a second venue. The only code SPM-81 changed is the AC4 rule below (built 2026-10-10, after the cases). All 11 cases passed when run by hand on 2026-10-11 (kayalvizhi24), on the build with main merged in.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (AC4, decided by kayalvizhi24): AC4 is followed as written. The same venue cannot be requested twice for the same EVENT at overlapping times, whichever session asks. This changes SPM-44's rule, which refused a repeat only for the same event AND the same session (PR #37 review; findDuplicateRequest() in src/lib/venueConflict.ts), so two sessions could hold one room at the same time. Sessions that only meet (one ends as the next starts) are still allowed, and the event's own bookings still never count as a clash with 'another event', so its setup and turnaround do not get in its own way. Covered by SPM-81-TC09.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (AC1, a room for part of the event): the rule that a request must cover the event's (or session's) whole time is kept (SPM-42, reworded by SPM-93). Reasons: Week 7 Change #3 and the user story both describe spaces used 'at the same time'; AC1 asks only for 'including for the same date and times'; AC8 says a single booking behaves as today; and a room needed for only part of the day already has a route: make that part a session (Week 4 multi-session events), which is booked for its own times. Requests may still be wider than the event. If the customer later asks for part-time rooms on an event without sessions, that is a new decision about what the first venue must cover.

DECIDED 2026-10-10 (AC6): 'shown together on the event' is the 'Booking requests' card on the event's Venue tab, which lists every request with its venue, times, layout and status, and the Overview's 'Venue' row, which names every approved room ('<room> (<code>) · <room> (<code>)', earliest start first). Both exist today, so no new screen or wording is added. A fuller list with outstanding/complete status belongs to Track Outstanding Arrangements (SPM-33, in progress), whose AC2 lists each venue booking separately.
DECIDED 2026-10-10: no new label, message or page address is introduced by these cases. Every quoted text is what the app shows today (SPM-42, SPM-43, SPM-44, SPM-93).

DECIDED 2026-10-10 (AC4 wording): when the room is held by a DIFFERENT session of the same event, the refusal says 'This event already has a pending request for <venue> on <date>, <times>.' (or '… already has <venue> booked on …' once approved), with the earlier request's own times. When the same session asks twice it still names the session ('Day 1 already has …'), as SPM-44 built it.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (AC7): only rejection is tested by hand here. No screen lets anyone change, withdraw or release a single venue booking yet: withdrawing and releasing are Withdraw or Release Venue Booking (SPM-67, To Do), whose description says the rule that the event's other bookings are unchanged 'is covered by SPM-81'. So when SPM-67 is built, its cases must include an event with two bookings and check that the other one is unchanged; until then that half of AC7 cannot be run by hand. Each booking is its own record and a decision writes only that record (automated tests assert this). A venue edit (SPM-39) or an event change (SPM-62) flags bookings for review rather than changing them, and has its own cases.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (out of scope, SPM-90): an event with one Approved and one Pending venue booking can still be confirmed, and submitted for a safety check, because both rules ask only whether a venue is held. 'Every required venue booking must be confirmed' is SPM-90's criterion, so no case here tries to confirm an event.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (#109 and #41): #109 said holding several candidate venues for one event was not required for Release 1; Week 7 Change #3 now requires several venues for one event. The system does not tell a candidate from a needed room: every pending request is a hold. #41 (one hold or booking per venue and overlapping period) is unchanged, because it is per venue.

For the team, not an SPM-81 criterion: the equipment availability check works out transfer time from 'the event's venue' and picks one (an approved booking first; src/lib/equipmentAvailabilityService.ts, venueFor()). With two rooms booked it is not defined which one the equipment goes to. SPM-90 records what each space is for, which may be the place to settle it.
